simple.meaning: רָטַשׁ (râṭâsh) is a Hebrew concept word meaning “to dash down.” BibleIQ follows how Scripture develops this idea across its occurrences.
simple.biblicalBackground: The concept appears 6 times across 2 Kings, Isaiah, Hosea, Nahum, beginning at 2 Kings 8:12. Its contexts include Israel.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to רָטַשׁ (H7376).
simple.whyItMatters: Concept words shape biblical themes. BibleIQ keeps the concept grounded in actual verse evidence instead of starting with a later theological definition.
simple.summary: רָטַשׁ (râṭâsh) / H7376 is traced through 2 Kings 8:12, Isaiah 13:16, Isaiah 13:18, Hosea 10:14 as a generated source-based concept entry.

firstOccurrence.englishText: Hazael said, “Why do you weep, my lord?”

timeline.evidenceText: Hazael said, “Why do you weep, my lord?”
Their infants also will be dashed in pieces before their eyes. Their houses will be ransacked, and their wives raped.
Their bows will dash the young men in pieces; and they shall have no pity on the fruit of the womb. Their eyes will not spare children.
Therefore a battle roar will arise among your people,
Israel, return to Yahweh your God;

Yet was she carried away. She went into captivity. Her young children also were dashed in pieces at the head of all the streets, and they cast lots for her honorable men, and all her great men were bound in chains.

definitions.full: H7376. ratash [ רָטַשׁ ] verb Pi`el dash in pieces (compare רְטַשׁ ᵑ7 cast away, reject; but possibly akin to לָטַשׁ ); — Pi`el Imperfect 2masculine singular תְּרַטֵּשׁ 2Kin 8:12 their children thou will dash in pieces ; 3 feminine plural תְּרַטַּשְׁנָה נְעָרִים קְשָׁתוֺת Isa 13:18 , but probably corrupt, Du conjecture תְּרֻטַּשְׁנָה נְעָרוֺת compare Che. Pu`al Perfect 3feminine singular רֻטָּ֑שָׁה בָּנִים עַלֿ אֵם Hosea 14:14; Imperfect 3masculine plural יְרֻטְּשׁוּ Isa 13:16 ; Nahum 3:10 , יְרֻטָּ֑שׁוּ Hosea 14:1 , all of children. רִי see רוה .
